To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the replica method can be applied to analyze MUD with imperfect channel estimation and that the system performance can be obtained in the large-system limit for optimal M UD, linear M UD and turbo M UD.

the channel estimation error has a negligible impact on the optimal multiuser detection (i.e. the performance loss is less than 0.5dB for a bit error rate of 10-5) and the channel estimation error is a dominant factor for linear and turbo multiuser detection (the performance degradation is about 1dB for a bit rate of 10−5).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the channel estimation error has little impact on the performance of MUD.
the impact of channel estimation on MUD is negligible in terms of the error probability, and the performance degradation caused by the channel estimation error is less than 1.5 dB.
the impact of channel estimation errors is not as significant as that of multiple-access interference.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the channel estimation error is not a serious problem for MUD in the large system limits, and the system performance is not much degraded even in the finite system case.
the channel estimation error is a major source of degradation to the performance of MUD in DS-CDMA wireless systems, especially when the number of users is large.
the impact of channel estimation errors on MUD performance is not as serious as the effect of multiple access interference, but is more severe for optimal MUD and linear MUD than for turbo MUD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the optimal MUD, the impact of channel estimation errors is similar to that of the noise.
the impact of channel estimation errors on the system performance is more severe than that on the bit error rate (BER).
the impact of imperfect channel estimation on system performance is not as significant as the impact of noise and interference.
